summary: Heavy steel tower, 24.4 m (80 ft); the 1963 move named in the sources may not be this structure, and no source describes the site today.

events.note: The Round Lake page says the Round Lake tower was dismantled and re-erected at Long Lake in 1963. This record reaches that page through the Round Lake name, but no source says the Round Hill structure is the same tower.
A towermen list places one observer across seven towers, Round Hill among them, for service from 1943 to 1963. The dates are that observer's service, not a start date for this tower.
A towermen list places one observer across six towers, Round Hill among them, for service from 1986 to 2001.

The 2013 sources describe a province-wide plan to end observers at 42 towers. None names Round Hill, so 'unstaffed' is not confirmed for this site.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The brief dates a relocation to this record through the Round Lake name. The Round Lake page says the Round Lake tower went to Long Lake that year. The story reports that page's statement and does not say the Round Hill structure moved.

notes_for_editor: Main open item is identity. The brief's 1963 'relocated' event and the Round Lake alias come from the Round Lake page, which says the Round Lake tower went to Long Lake. The survey lists a heavy steel tower at Round Hill with no build year, so the sources do not show whether it is the same structure; the story states only what the Round Lake page says. Observer names are left out of the story and JSON: the local websiteservice source says towermen names are not stored. No source describes the site today or gives access rules. The brief's 'unstaffed' line and its 2013-14 note are province-wide; none of the sources names Round Hill among the 42 towers. The 'formerly Dept. of Natural Resources' clause is not supported (see corrections).
